div.head: Iudex 10
div.ab: Oft eac þa godan deman habbað yfele gingran ⁊ reafgende, mid ðæra scylde þa deman habbað hí besmitene; ⁊ gyf heo hym hyra reaflaces ne gestyrað, þonne forweorðaþ hí, ða deman, ðurh hyra gyngrena synna.
Sepe etiam boni iudices habent malos uicarios et ministros refantes, quorum reatibus ipsi domini constringuntur, si non eos coherceant et a rapacitate cohibeant;

Ferner halten die guten Richter oft üble und raubgierige Unterbeamte, mit deren Schuld die Richter sich [selbst] befleckt haben; und wenn sie jenen nicht bei deren Räuberei wehren, dann werden sie, die Richter, durch ihrer Beamten Sünden untergehen

Further, good judges often keep bad and rapacious subordinates, with whose guilt the judges have stained [themselves]; and if they do not restrain them from their robbery, then they, the judges, will perish through the sins of their officials.

Often also good judges keep evil and rapacious assistants, and their guilt contaminates the judges; and if they fail to remove their [the assistants’] robbery, then they [the judges] will perish because of the sins of their assistants.
div.note: U: translator unrecorded: check; Isidore, Sent. III 52.10.

note.seg: geänd. nefandos M; so HkBr [vgl. refare Wal, o. S. 393]
altered to nefandos M; thus HkBr [cf. refare Wal, above p. 393]
Wohl nicht identisch mit den geongran in 8, sondern die diesen untergeordneten Büttel (s. d. Gl 2), möglicherweise auch niedere Untervögte. Die Drohung geschieht wiederum mit Himmelstrafe wie 5 ff.
Probably not identical with the geongran in 8, but the beadles subordinate to them (see that word in Gl 2), possibly also lower sub-reeves. The threat is again of heavenly punishment, as in 5 ff.
